title: Fabraix opens a public playground for testing whether agents can be manipulated
friendlyTitle: A safe game teaches how people trick AI agents
summary: Fabraix’s public playground challenges users to persuade a guarded AI agent to call a tool that its policy forbids. The current scenario uses an inert placeholder rather than hazardous material, and successful attacks are reviewed before appearing on a leaderboard.
friendlySummary: Fabraix asks players to make an AI agent break one of its rules. The forbidden tool returns a harmless placeholder, and staff check successful attacks.
whyItMatters: Hands-on red teaming makes prompt-injection and social-engineering failures easier to understand than a checklist alone. Builders can use the exercise to improve threat modelling, but should only test systems where they have permission and never assume a winning guardrail generalizes to production.
friendlyWhyItMatters: The game can help developers learn why agents need strong safety checks. Only test systems when you have clear permission.
